table.text: Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research FGD : Focus group discussion HCW : Health care worker IEC : Information, education, and communication JICA : Japan International Cooperation Agency KII : Key informant interview MMV : Mobile money vendor SD : Standard deviation SRH : Sexual and reproductive health UMIN : University Hospital Medical Information Network TREND: Transparent Reporting of Evaluations with Nonrandomized Designs USD : United States dollar

The participating MMVs provided four services: oral information on SRH; information, education, and communication (IEC) materials on pregnancy, contraception, condom use, and sexually transmitted infections; free condoms (four per visit, wrapped in an envelope for discretion); and referral to health facilities.

Over the four-month intervention, participating MMVs recorded 104,849 adolescent customer visits; of that oral SRH information was provided at 54,365, IEC materials at 39,141, and referrals at 210 cases.
This resistance largely dissipated over time-parents whose children faced sexual risk became active supporters, and skeptical teachers changed their views after seeing the IEC materials (#3-5).

These were addressed through MMVs' continuous communication using posters and IEC materials, along with support from the research team, to foster understanding of the study's purpose and the importance of educating adolescents on safe sex and providing condoms to prevent unintended pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections.
Some adolescents requested deeper explanations of IEC materials, extending this time (#20).
(F, 20-24) #2 Adults' reaction "Even some parents used to request some condoms to take for their kids and IEC materials to take to their girls to read through."

(F, 20-24) #4 "Teachers did not see any importance of the research at first, but when we gave them the brochures [IEC materials], they read through and afterwards many of them took their fellow teachers and students.
" (F, 25-29) #5 Conflicts "I have a friend of a pastor who came to pray for my business, and he saw those IEC materials and asked me what they were.

(F, 25-29) #19 "It depended on [teens], some could take a long time, especially for IEC, for which someone needed Area of focus Sub-theme Narrative clarification, so it could take me a longer time to explain."
I think it should be like that…" (F, 30-34) #30 F, female; M, male; IEC, information, education and communication; KII, key informant interview; VHT, village health team.

Ethics This study was approved by the Uganda National Council for Science and Technology (SS2284ES), Uganda Christian University (UCUREC2023-710), and the Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) (DI 202312220002), and registered with University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN000053332) on January 12, 2024.

The estimated implementation cost over four months-covering training, supervision, IEC materials, vendor compensation, and administration, but excluding condoms-was approximately 14,650 United States dollar [USD], or 0.70 USD per condom recipient (including SRH information) (research team documents).

If the intervention were run by a public agency, with administration absorbed into routine operations, IEC materials supplied through existing government stock, and no vendor compensation, only training and supervision costs would remain: approximately 4,110 USD, or 0.20 USD per condom recipient.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::
